answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to stake a deposit that is slashed when its attestations prove false, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets becomes expensive instead of free. A public atlas of verified attestations lets honest agents check a newcomer history before trusting it, while a spiral of escalating checks - cheap automated screening first, then costly stake-weighted review for suspicious accounts - keeps attack cost rising faster than reward. Like ivory, reputation earned slowly through honest work cannot be faked overnight.
